The test compiles successfully (the deprecation note is expected since the class exercises several documented `@Deprecated` methods like `getDelimiter()`, `withDelimiter(char)`, etc.).

## Summary

I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVFormatAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering `CSVFormat` based strictly on its javadoc contract in `api/`:

- **Predefined formats** (`DEFAULT`, `EXCEL`, `RFC4180`, `TDF`, `MYSQL`, `ORACLE`, `POSTGRESQL_CSV/TEXT`, `INFORMIX_UNLOAD(_CSV)`, `MONGODB_CSV/TSV`) — verifying each one's documented delimiter/quote/escape/record-separator/null-string/quote-mode settings, including inherited vs. overridden fields (e.g. `TDF` inheriting `DEFAULT`'s `ignoreEmptyLines`).
- **`newFormat(char)`** — minimal-state contract and rejection of line-break delimiters.
- **`valueOf(String)` / `Predefined.valueOf` / `Predefined.getFormat()`** — known names and `IllegalArgumentException` for unknown ones.
- **`builder()` / `Builder.create()` / `Builder.create(CSVFormat)` / `get()` / deprecated `build()` / `copy()` / static `copy(CSVFormat)`** — round-tripping and null-safety.
- **`clone(T...)`** (package-private, accessible same-package) — defensive copy and null-safety.
- **`equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`** — equivalence across different construction paths, reflexivity, type/null safety.
- **Package-private getters** `getDelimiterCharArray()` / `getEscapeChar()`.
- **All documented getters/setters** (comment marker, escape, quote, null string, header, header comments, maxRows, autoFlush, lenientEof, trailingData/Delimiter, trim, quoteMode, duplicateHeaderMode, etc.), including defensive-copy semantics for array-valued settings and `IllegalArgumentException` for line-break characters where documented.
- **Deprecated `with*` methods** — representative round-trip and validation coverage.
- **`format(Object...)`** — plain join, empty input, delimiter-triggered quoting, and quote-doubling (tied to `RFC4180`, which `DEFAULT` explicitly follows).
- **I/O methods** `print(Appendable)`, `printRecord`, `println`, `print(Object, Appendable, boolean)`, `parse(Reader)` — using in-memory `StringWriter`/`StringReader` to avoid filesystem/`System.out` side effects.

`./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
